candidates.text:
there's a louis ck bit. it's basically like, if a man wakes up and discovers all humans are gone, how long until he starts having sex with the animals?

he goes on to talk about which animals. then he pauses and he's like, but i guess. you know. how sure do you have to be that you're the last man on earth? before you have sex with the animals? like. how long would you look around?

it's a great joke because it starts with the thought exercise of being the last man on earth. and then it basically tears down thought exercises themselves

how could you know? how could you ever know? the earth is enormous. and hostile. how exactly would you ever know?

the joke is not about the animals. it's that you should spend your entire life looking for the any other fucking human

the rationalists have many thought exercises where they end up with the animals

it's the same shape as the chappelle joke. "he rapes, but he saves". ok well. did he see if there was anything he could do before he raped? did he check if there was anything else that might have activated his saving powers?

i get the thought exercises. i see the point you're driving me to. but it's just not going to be simulated correctly. and that's true all over the fucking place

the eas do all these thought exercises and believe they are rational. and all the thought exercises are like, ok you're in a world where this is true. or, you're in a game where these are the rules.

a lot of people don't come up with the solutions that the rationalists like but to be honest, that's because their prior on the probability, or like, the rationality of that construct, is so low. they can't even conceive of it really. they can't do the thought exercise.

i sort of think people are rational in different ways.

some people are like yeah man. i just don't really believe i'm in a game with those rules. or: i don't believe i'm in a game. you know? right? they refuse that framing of reality. that framing of reality is extremely alien to them.

framing is very powerful. and it's rarely neutral. i appreciate the eas, this is not a criticism of the eas, all humans do it.

humans are like, step into my frame. we're going to have this rational neutral discussion and we are agreeing this is the rational neutral framing. and whatever the framing is, it's not as rational and neutral and honest as they might want you to think it is.

it's meant to skew you one way or the other by being pulled into that frame. frames carry with them implicit baggage. or moral obligations, or social constructs, or a billion other pesky human things that leave you less rational and less reasonable than you normally would be. it manipulates you into seeing or thinking a certain way.

that does not mean the frames are insidious or dangerous or nefarious. it's just, not neutral.

so, look. i can play the game. but how do we know we're in the game? like, how do we? why are we talking about fucking animals until we've established what we really know? might i suggest we check to see if there's more humans first.

if we've accepted the framing where the rules of the game are that the ais are going to be smarter than humans, and we just believed that, would we not have thrown the compute at it earlier?

until there was the first llm, it wasn't that clear. like how these things scale with compute. and also, whether there was a product you could attach to it that would be useful to people.

we kind of forget now, but i actually think ultimately google had to come first. before an llm could feel useful to people

the original ea thing was that you don't invest where there are no returns. that capitalism demands a charitable sidecar of sorts. i think different rationalists have different opinions on how large the sidecar is.

but, for example. back in like 2015, husband worked with a guy who was invited to the US from a not-rich country, on merit scholarships. think of the most exceptional things you could have done in the very most objective disciplines, and the most elite schools that would get you into, back when that still meant something. because remember, this is 2015.

husband was reading about this still fairly nascent philosophy, and he told the guy about the eas

the guy replies, "but why would you value a human life?"

forget the fucking shrimps man.

if we are immediately jumping to the conclusion that the rules of the game are that the robots will obsolete us then. well. i don't know.

eventually obviously with infinite compute and infinite search, basically the humans won't compete. and of course it's beyond our wildest imaginations right now. compute and search have gone up so fast. we've thrown so much more compute and power at these problems that of course the results are shocking to us. it's like a fucking j curve on how much we're spending on compute. and maybe we continue to do that. can we keep it up forever? i don't know.

there's part of me that thinks the real win of this whole cycle is just that, ok yeah, i guess it wasn't that hard to build data centers. it's the elon way. first principles, brute force. no pussyfooting around. i think that's pretty much my view

we just jerked off for 20, 30 years and did nothing. that's why we didn't have ai. if only we'd fucking convinced ourselves, you just need shitloads of compute to massively transform what computers can do for humans.

human beings have been writing code so that other human beings can clearly understand the code and we have a good understanding of what human beings understand and what they don't.

a senior engineer can look at a code base and if you ask them, hey what are the missing abstractions, they can look at it and be like, hmm yeah. we can rethink how we do the config management. by extracting this concept out, and doing this, that, and the other. the ais are only now starting to get decent at that.

and of course, the argument is that soon it doesn't matter. because you can already get things to work without necessarily solving it the same way humans do. we humans need all these abstractions and encapsulations because we can only keep so much complexity in our mind. our context windows are small.

i don't think my opinion on this has changed. eventually all human code will be legacy code to be cleaned up. because it's going to be so different than the way the robots operate.

but right now, the way the robots think about problems and the way the humans think about problems are still deeply decoupled. because of our relative strengths currently. the humans still believe, however haplessly, that problems can be solved.

a year ago, i did notes on hitchhiker's guide to the galaxy. i wrote how, at the beginning of the book, the stupid human is accepting his fate and, just, laying down in the mud to fucking die.

meanwhile, the unflappable alien is very much unstuck. he is kicking hatches, hitting switches, making moves and BELIEVING THAT MOVES CAN BE MADE.

when you think about it, how are the ais solving all the math proofs? lol, well. the humans are sitting there saying: just do it. you can do it.

the robots still require us dumb human cheerleaders. the ai agents have no fucking agency. the humans still gave the swarm the unsolvable problem to solve. maybe the robots will accidentally kill all humans. i don't know. but i'm not sure i believe they'll be intelligent afterwards

skill issue if you need peptides or whatever. here’s how you can mog without them:

literally just do 500kcal daily deficit which is super manageable to do and over a period of 6-12 months makes a huge difference. easiest way to do is to have 2-3 slop bowl places you can spam daily for 95% of your meals (for me it’s chipotle, mixt and this niche spot called tacko in the marina). 500kcal/day deficit is about -1lb/week. if you wanna drop 10lbs, just do it for 10 weeks. great thing about slop bowl places is you can build your bowls like lego blocks (get 2x-3x scoops of protein when u need, or get 0.5x scoops of rice etc)

add a daily step goal, just try to walking to work and back. if you’re into distance running, then zone 2 running is a good addition but not needed if you’re not into it. i have been doing avg 12-15miles/week since late 2024, mainly cause i enjoy it and find that endurance training makes me better at certain things in life that are actually hard like startups. it will make you hungrier tho so i wouldn’t recommend it if your goal is purely to lean out. biking is also a good addition 

make sure to lift weights regularly to retain muscle. you will lose some strength but you need to retain muscle because that’s how you mog. i was fortunate to have a decent muscle base to start cause i have been lifting since college, just wasn’t good about eating right

i think more important than hardcore discipline, what you need is a system so dumb and easy to follow that it’s impossible to mess up. another thing you need is patience for like the first few months, cause people around you don’t notice change immediately so it’s easy to think you’re not making progress. but you feel so good on the system you keep going and then eventually people notice

candidates.text:
Nasdaq's Director of Communications for their "Digital Liquidity Networks" org  role is a peek into the future: 
- continuous, always-on trading 
- programmable market structures 
- tokenization 

I started wondering when Nasdaq and NYSE tokenize equities, how they will execute. Will it be fragmented order books? And does it directly compete with the xStocks, Ondo stocks, Robinhood token stocks, Dinari stocks today?

I looked into the SEC releases and found out both Nasdaq and NYSE are launching tokenized equities with  unified liquidity - both tokenized and traditional shares will trade on the same order book 

This however, won't be DeFi. It's walled gardens, permissioned finance on crypto rails

For reaching offshore non-US people: 
- Nasdaq is partnering with xStocks (Kraken/Payward) on an equities gateway that converts DTCC custodied equities to tokenized forms
- NYSE is launching a new 24/7 venue for tokenized securities

Both of these efforts bring flow back to the underlying US capital markets. Crypto rails create access and extend distribution to global capital, similar to stablecoins increasing demand for the dollar or Fasanara getting new investors on their Global Diversified Alternative Debt Fund with Midas. These also both seem to be competitors to existing tokenized equity options that exist today, with full defi composability - but will not merely be wrappers

There's three levels of blockchain finance emerging: 
1. Existing finance importing controlled, blockchain infrastructure (walled gardens) 
2. Permissioned DeFi: whitelisted assets, AML/KYC/KYB, for accredited investors only but usable in composable onchain markets
3. Fully permissionless DeFi
